blocks.text: Your inventory tracking spreadsheet serves as the backbone of your operations. Whether you use Excel for Mac or Google Sheets, the logic remains the same. Start with a single sheet for your product list. Include columns for SKU, item name, unit cost, and current stock level. Avoid merging cells, as this breaks sorting and filtering later. Keep your headers in the first row. Use the Freeze Panes feature in Excel by going to View > Freeze Panes > Freeze Top Row to keep your headers visible while you scroll through hundreds of rows.

Manual entry is the primary source of inventory discrepancies. If you type a SKU wrong, your stock count fails. Use Data Validation to restrict inputs. In Excel, select your range, then go to Data > Data Validation. Choose List from the Allow menu. This ensures users pick from a predefined list rather than typing free text. If you are using Google Sheets, the path is Data > Data validation. This small step saves hours of cleanup time later in the month.

Automation relies on formulas. Use SUMIF to calculate total stock sold across different warehouses. For example, =SUMIF(A:A, "SKU123", C:C) adds up all values in column C where column A matches your specific SKU. This is much faster than manual counting. If you need to compare two columns in Excel on Mac, use conditional formatting to highlight duplicates or missing items. This visual check prevents stockouts before they happen. Always verify your ranges before applying complex formulas to large datasets.
Optimizing your daily workflow on Mac

Inventory managers often switch between multiple apps like Zoho Inventory, Odoo, or QuickBooks Online. Each app has its own navigation structure. Using ⌥ ⌘ (Option + Command) with Lazur lets you ask where a specific setting is located. If you are lost in a deep menu, ask Lazur to point at the button. It draws a circle around the target, saving you from hunting through help menus. This is particularly helpful when you are under pressure to process purchase orders quickly.

Email remains a constant interruption. When you receive a supplier update, you must act fast. Hold fn to dictate your replies directly into Outlook or Mail. Keeping your hands on the keyboard keeps your flow state intact. If you find yourself spending too much time drafting standard responses, use the dictation feature to quickly capture your thoughts. Remember that focus takes 23 minutes to regain after an interruption. Protect your time by grouping your email tasks into specific blocks during the day.

items: Perform a physical stock count at least once a month to verify your spreadsheet data.
Use unique SKUs for every item to avoid confusion.
Back up your files to iCloud or another secure drive every day.
Keep your spreadsheet file size small by removing unused formatting.
Check your formulas for errors after adding new rows of data.

blocks.text: The most common mistake is failing to update the spreadsheet immediately after a shipment arrives. Delayed updates lead to inaccurate stock levels. Another issue is using the wrong cell references in formulas. If you move rows, ensure your formulas still point to the correct data. Always test your formulas with a small sample of data before applying them to your entire master inventory list. If a formula returns an error, use the Formula Auditing tools in Excel to trace the source of the problem.
